children: The manager of the country's $2.3 trln sovereign fund may reduce American government debt to 22% of its bond index, from 34% now. Yet it's mostly a way to buy more US state-backed mortgage securities instead. Diversifying away from dollar assets, including equities too, is hard.

The manager of Norway's $2.3 trillion sovereign wealth fund has proposed significantly cutting its exposure to U.S. Treasuries as part of a wider shake-up of its bond investments to improve returns, according to a letter sent to the country's finance ministry on September 1.
Norges Bank Investment Management has recommended reducing its weighting to government bonds within its benchmark bond index to 50% from 70%.
"We recommend that the government subindex of the bond index be reduced from 70% to 50%," Ida Wolden Bache, governor of Norges Bank, and Norges Bank IM CEO Nicolai Tangen wrote in the letter.
"A government share of 50% will be sufficient to cover the liquidity needs, including in periods of turbulence in financial markets."

While U.S. Treasuries exposure would fall, the proposed allocation to U.S. non-government debt would jump from 16.2% to 27.6%, meaning that the overall bond index's weighting to the U.S. dollar would fall only slightly, from 52.9% to 52.5%.
